title: Rewrite docs/explainers/sync-subsystem.md — it still presents the deleted SyncEngine/OfflineQueue dual-stack as the live, highest-risk architecture

evidence.quote: the legacy `SyncEngine`. Several thousand lines, the largest single file in `features/sync/`, marked `@deprecated` and still load-bearing.
`learning_order` has no `EntityMerger` in the new stack — the orchestrator's pull silently merges nothing for that collection

why: git log shows commit e14479af "refactor(sync): delete SyncEngine, OfflineQueue, FirestoreDataSource — W2.35-W2.39": grepping lib/ for SyncEngine/OfflineQueue/sync_engine.dart today returns zero hits. learning_order_merger.dart exists and is wired in merge_router.dart's switch (18 case labels = 18 concrete *_merger.dart files, not the doc's claimed 8). An engineer or AI agent reading this doc to understand sync architecture — the coding-standards.md digest itself calls core/sync/** the area needing "Nygard lens mandatory" scrutiny — will hunt for a deleted file, misjudge risk, and may re-attempt a decomposition that is already finished, or skip auditing the 10 mergers the doc doesn't mention.
recommendation: Regenerate this explainer against current lib/core/sync/: drop the two-stack narrative entirely (SyncEngine is gone), correct the EntityMerger count to the actual count of *_merger.dart files, and remove the learning_order "sharp edge" (closed by W2.26). Re-verify the other two "known sharp edges" (curriculum-import collection naming — already renamed per firestore_gateway_impl.dart:617; DriftMergeStore.currentUpdatedAt nullability) before republishing.
acceptance_criteria: Doc no longer references features/sync/data/sync_engine.dart, SyncEngine, or OfflineQueue as live/current.
EntityMerger count and the merge/ file listing match `ls learning_tracker/lib/core/sync/merge/*_merger.dart | grep -v entity_merger.dart | wc -l`.
The "as of 2026-05-19" disclaimer date is bumped to the doc's actual re-verification date.
Optional but recommended: a CI/doc-lint script asserts the merger count named in the doc equals the file-count above, failing non-zero on drift (operationalizes AG-8 for this doc).
